name: D8 Visa (Digital Nomad)

requirements.blocker_text: This requires remote income from foreign employers/clients of at least €3,680/month (4x the 2026 minimum wage).
requirements.fix_path: Increase remote income to the required level.

value.note: approximately 12 months of the RMMG-based threshold; consular practice, higher for accompanying dependents

requirements.blocker_text: This requires savings of approximately €11,040 (roughly 12 months of the base threshold), consular practice rather than a fixed statutory figure.
requirements.fix_path: Build savings to the expected level.

requirements.blocker_text: This requires the income to come from clients or an employer based outside Portugal.

evidence_required.document: Employment contract or freelance client contracts showing foreign-sourced income
Bank statements showing the required savings buffer

outcome.duration_length: 4-month entry visa, then 2-year residence permit, renewable

sources.title: Portal de Vistos - Ministério dos Negócios Estrangeiros

notes: FORMULA VALUE, tier-1 confirmed: exactly 4x RMMG, same reference variable as pt_d7. IMPORTANT STRUCTURAL NOTE, not yet fully modeled: Portugal actually has TWO distinct D8 products — a temporary-stay visa (valid up to 1 year, renewable, does NOT count toward permanent residence or citizenship at all) and this residency-visa variant. This file encodes ONLY the residency variant, since it's the one with real long-term immigration value; the temporary-stay variant is a genuinely different product with a different outcome (leads_to_pr: false) that would need its own file for full accuracy — flagged as a scope decision, not an oversight, since the temporary variant is closer to an extended-tourism product than an immigration route. Anyone switching from a foreign employer to a Portuguese one must convert to a D1 work permit — D8 income must remain genuinely foreign-sourced throughout. Same 84-month citizenship figure and same CPLP/EU vs other-nationality caveat as pt_d7.
